project.name: Dynamic Data Processing and Output Workflow

sections.title: Project Overview
sections.content: The Dynamic Data Processing and Output Workflow project aims to streamline and automate data handling through a series of interconnected workflows. Each workflow is designed to efficiently process data from entry to exit, ensuring data integrity and operational efficiency.

sections.title: Goals & Objectives
sections.content:
1. Automate data processing to reduce manual intervention.
2. Ensure high data integrity and accuracy.
3. Optimize workflow efficiency and reduce processing time.
4. Provide clear entry and exit points for each workflow.

sections.title: System Architecture
sections.content: The system architecture consists of four distinct workflows, each with a specific entry and exit point. Workflows are interconnected through nodes and connections, facilitating seamless data transitions and processing.

sections.title: Workflow Summary
sections.content:
## Ticket Review and Zigalert Creation Workflow

Purpose: Assists the Mission Controller in evaluating tickets, confirming their validity, and initiating Zigalerts.

Objective: Optimize the handling of valid tickets to ensure prompt Zigalert creation, thereby enhancing response efficiency.

User: Mission Controller (MC).

Result: Valid tickets lead to the creation and publication of Zigalerts, with closed and linked tickets maintained for tracking purposes.



## Duplicate Ticket Handling Workflow

Purpose: Offers a systematic approach for the Mission Controller to identify and link duplicate tickets or proceed with validation if no duplicates are found.

Objective: Minimize redundancy by linking duplicates to existing Zigalerts while ensuring new issues are appropriately addressed.

User: Mission Controller (MC).

Result: Duplicate tickets are linked and closed, reducing clutter, while unique tickets proceed to validation.



## Closed Ticket Search and Reopen Workflow

Purpose: Allows the Mission Controller to review closed tickets and determine if they require reopening for further action.

Objective: Enable retrospective evaluation and action on tickets needing additional attention or correction.

User: Mission Controller (MC).

Result: Tickets can be reopened for immediate triage or re-entered into the queue for standard processing.

These workflows enhance the Mission Controller's efficiency and accuracy in ticket management, ensuring timely and precise issue resolution.

sections.title: Assumptions
sections.content:
1. All workflows are independent yet can be integrated for comprehensive data processing.
2. Nodes and connections are pre-defined and optimized for specific data tasks.
3. Entry and exit points are clearly defined and consistent across workflows.
4. System resources are sufficient to handle the processing load of all workflows.

prdSections.title: Overview
prdSections.content: Workflow 1 is designed to manage the process of handling FleetSense tickets, ensuring that each ticket is reviewed, triaged, and appropriately closed or linked to existing alerts.

prdSections.title: Requirements
prdSections.content: The system must allow MC to check open FleetSense tickets, select 'Pending Approval' tickets, review the success of ZigAlert creation, triage tickets, validate them, and determine the appropriate closure or linking actions.

prdSections.title: User Flow
prdSections.content: 1. MC checks open FleetSense tickets. 2. MC selects a 'Pending Approval' ticket. 3. MC reviews if the system was successful in creating a valid ZigAlert. 4. If not successful, MC checks for duplicates. 5. If duplicate, MC links it to an existing ZA. 6. If not duplicate, MC triages the ticket. 7. MC validates the ticket. 8. If valid and requires ZA, MC creates a ZA and closes the ticket. 9. If not valid, MC marks it as invalid and closes the ticket.

prdSections.title: Inputs & Outputs
prdSections.content: Inputs: Open FleetSense tickets, 'Pending Approval' tickets. Outputs: Closed tickets, linked duplicates, created ZigAlerts.

prdSections.title: Failure Scenarios
prdSections.content: 1. System fails to retrieve open tickets. 2. Incorrect ticket selection due to UI issues. 3. Error in determining ZigAlert creation success. 4. Duplicate detection failure. 5. Incorrect validation leading to wrong ticket closure.

prdSections.title: Recovery & Fallback Paths
prdSections.content: 1. Implement retry logic for ticket retrieval. 2. Provide manual override for ticket selection errors. 3. Log errors in ZigAlert creation for review. 4. Allow manual duplicate linking if automatic detection fails. 5. Enable re-validation of tickets if closure is incorrect.

prdSections.title: Operational Risks
prdSections.content: 1. High volume of tickets may lead to performance degradation. 2. Monitoring required for duplicate detection accuracy. 3. Regular audits needed to ensure correct ticket closure.

prdSections.title: Acceptance Criteria
prdSections.content: 1. All 'Pending Approval' tickets can be processed through the workflow. 2. Successful creation of ZigAlerts for valid tickets. 3. Accurate detection and linking of duplicate tickets. 4. All invalid tickets are correctly marked and closed.

prdSections.title: Overview
prdSections.content: Workflow 2 is designed to manage the review and processing of tickets by the Mission Controller (MC). It involves reviewing tickets, checking their validity, and creating and publishing alerts if necessary.

prdSections.title: Requirements
prdSections.content: The system must allow the Mission Controller to review tickets, determine their validity, and either close them as invalid or proceed to create and publish alerts. The workflow should seamlessly transition between nodes based on ticket validity.

prdSections.title: User Flow
prdSections.content: 1. Mission Controller begins review (Start). 2. MC reviews the ticket for validity (Review Ticket). 3. System checks if the ticket is valid (Check Validity). 4. If valid, create a hazard alert (Create Zigalert). 5. Publish the created alert (Publish Zigalert). 6. Link ticket to alert and close (Close and Link Ticket). 7. If invalid, mark ticket as invalid and close (Mark Invalid & Close).

prdSections.title: Inputs & Outputs
prdSections.content: Inputs: Ticket details from Mission Controller. Outputs: Invalid ticket closure, published Zigalert, linked ticket to alert.

prdSections.title: Failure Scenarios
prdSections.content: 1. Ticket validity is incorrectly assessed, leading to wrong alert creation. 2. System fails to create or publish Zigalert due to connectivity issues. 3. Errors in linking ticket to Zigalert. 4. Unexpected system downtime during any process.

prdSections.title: Recovery & Fallback Paths
prdSections.content: 1. Implement retry logic for publishing alerts in case of failure. 2. Provide manual override for Mission Controller to reassess ticket validity. 3. Log errors and notify support for manual intervention. 4. Ensure system has failover capabilities to handle downtime.

prdSections.title: Operational Risks
prdSections.content: 1. Risk of false alerts affecting public safety. 2. Need for continuous monitoring of system performance and alert accuracy. 3. Ensure data integrity during ticket processing and alert publication.

prdSections.title: Acceptance Criteria
prdSections.content: 1. Tickets are accurately reviewed and processed. 2. Valid tickets result in correct alert creation and publication. 3. Invalid tickets are closed without alert creation. 4. System handles errors gracefully with minimal downtime.

prdSections.title: Overview
prdSections.content: Workflow 3 is designed to manage ticket reviews, assess duplicates, validate tickets, and create Zigalerts. It involves 10 nodes and aims to streamline ticket handling by identifying duplicates and invalid tickets early in the process.

prdSections.title: Requirements
prdSections.content: The workflow must efficiently process tickets, identify duplicates, validate ticket information, and manage Zigalert creation and publication. It should handle both valid and invalid tickets appropriately, ensuring accurate ticket closure and linking.

prdSections.title: User Flow
prdSections.content: 1. Start reviewing ticket. 2. Check for duplicates. 3. If duplicate, link and close as duplicate. 4. If not a duplicate, validate the ticket. 5. If valid, create and publish a Zigalert, then close and link the ticket. 6. If invalid, mark the ticket as invalid and close.

prdSections.title: Inputs & Outputs
prdSections.content: Inputs: Ticket information from 'Start'. Outputs: Closed ticket, linked duplicate, published Zigalert, or marked invalid ticket.

prdSections.title: Failure Scenarios
prdSections.content: Potential failure scenarios include incorrect duplicate detection, validation errors, failure to create or publish Zigalerts, and incorrect ticket closure. Edge cases involve tickets with incomplete data or ambiguous duplicate status.

prdSections.title: Recovery & Fallback Paths
prdSections.content: The system should log errors and provide alerts for manual intervention. Retry logic should be implemented for Zigalert creation and publishing. If validation fails, the ticket should be flagged for review.

prdSections.title: Operational Risks
prdSections.content: Risks include system downtime affecting ticket processing, incorrect duplicate or validation results, and failure in Zigalert publication. Monitoring should be in place for node transitions and error rates.

prdSections.title: Acceptance Criteria
prdSections.content: The workflow should correctly identify and process duplicates, validate tickets accurately, and ensure Zigalerts are created and published without errors. All exit points must be reachable based on ticket conditions.

prdSections.title: Overview
prdSections.content: Workflow 4 is designed to manage the process of reviewing and potentially reopening closed tickets. It consists of six nodes that guide the user from searching closed tickets to deciding whether to reopen them, and finally directing the ticket to the appropriate next step.

prdSections.title: Requirements
prdSections.content: The system must allow users to search through historical closed tickets, review them, make decisions on reopening, and handle the ticket accordingly. The workflow should be intuitive and efficient, minimizing the time spent on each ticket.

prdSections.title: User Flow
prdSections.content: 1. User searches closed tickets. 2. User selects a ticket for review. 3. User decides whether to reopen the ticket. 4. If reopened, the ticket is either sent back to the queue or enters triage mode.

prdSections.title: Inputs & Outputs
prdSections.content: Inputs: Closed tickets database. Outputs: Updated ticket status, either in queue or in triage mode.

prdSections.title: Failure Scenarios
prdSections.content: 1. Search returns no results due to incorrect query. 2. Decision to reopen is made incorrectly due to lack of information. 3. Reopen process fails due to system error. 4. Incorrect routing to Back to Queue or Triage Mode.

prdSections.title: Recovery & Fallback Paths
prdSections.content: 1. Implement retry logic for failed searches. 2. Provide additional information or context to aid decision-making. 3. Log errors and provide user feedback for failed reopen attempts. 4. Allow manual override for routing errors.

prdSections.title: Operational Risks
prdSections.content: 1. High volume of tickets could lead to performance issues. 2. Monitoring needed for decision accuracy and system errors. 3. Ensure data integrity when updating ticket statuses.

prdSections.title: Acceptance Criteria
prdSections.content: 1. Users can successfully search and select closed tickets. 2. Decision to reopen is logged and executed correctly. 3. Tickets are accurately routed to Back to Queue or Triage Mode. 4. System handles errors gracefully and provides feedback to users.
